oneLiner: The AI compute monopoly-in-practice: ~92% of revenue is data center, growing 85%+ with 75% gross margins, priced at a below-market forward multiple that assumes sharp deceleration.
thesis: CUDA plus full-system integration (GPU + Vera CPU + NVLink + racks) remains the deepest lock-in in semis; the annual Hopper-Blackwell-Rubin cadence keeps rivals aiming at a moving target.
Hyperscaler capex is estimated around $725B in 2026 (vs ~$410B in 2025) with ~$1T projected for 2027; NVDA captures the largest single share of that spend.

Forward P/E of ~22-24x is below the trailing multiple and below the 30-40x band of 2023-2025: the market is already pricing sharp deceleration, so the debate is about duration of the capex cycle, not the multiple.
China is effectively a free option: H200 licenses exist (~$10B approved) but Beijing has blocked purchases; current numbers embed roughly zero China revenue.

latestQuarter.label: Q1 FY2027 (ended Apr 26, 2026; reported May 20, 2026)
points: Revenue $81.6B, +85% YoY, +20% QoQ (~$2.8B above Street); Data Center $75.2B, +92% YoY.
GAAP gross margin 74.9%; operating margin 65.6% (operating income $53.5B, +147% YoY).
GAAP diluted EPS $2.39 (+214% YoY); non-GAAP $1.87 (now includes stock comp).
Guide: Q2 FY2027 revenue $91.0B plus or minus 2%, gross margin ~75%. Dividend raised to $0.25/q; $80B added to buyback.
Edge Computing segment (Gaming + ProViz + Auto) $6.4B, ~8% of revenue, +29% YoY.

segments: Data Center ~92% of revenue ($75.2B in Q1 FY27): Blackwell/GB300 is the volume platform; Rubin layers in H2 2026.
Edge Computing ~8% ($6.4B): Gaming $3.7B (+47%), Professional Visualization $1.3B, Automotive $604M (+6%).
competitive: AMD MI400 series narrows the hardware gap but trails on software ecosystem.
Custom ASICs are the most credible threat: Broadcom (Google TPU, Meta MTIA, OpenAI), Marvell (Trainium, Maia) take share-of-wallet at the largest, most concentrated buyers.
Cerebras (CBRS) IPO'd May 2026 with a 750MW OpenAI deal: small revenue but a validated wafer-scale inference alternative.
Hyperscaler in-house silicon (TPU v7, Trainium 3, Maia 2) grows faster than merchant GPUs in 2026 (TrendForce: +45% vs +16%).
moat: CUDA and the surrounding software stack, compounded by full-system integration competitors must replicate across six-plus co-designed chips, an annual platform cadence, and a 350+-factory supply chain ramped for Rubin.
risks: Customer concentration: three direct customers were 21%, 17% and 16% of Q1 FY27 revenue (54% combined).
AI capex cycle: any hyperscaler digestion pause hits NVDA disproportionately; 2027 capex guidance this fall is the swing factor.
China effectively zero: H200 licensed but unbought; Blackwell-derivative China status unclear.
Custom silicon substitution at precisely the three concentrated customers.
Power constraints: US data center power demand projected ~66GW in 2027 vs ~31GW in 2026.
Rubin execution: first shipments Q3 2026, volume Q4 2026; slippage hits FY2028 estimates.
catalysts: Rubin first shipments Q3 2026; volume ramp Q4 2026 (Microsoft, AWS, Google Cloud, CoreWeave named early adopters).
pricedIn: At ~$218, implied forward EPS is roughly $9-10 (22-24x forward vs ~32x trailing). Paying a market-plus multiple for 85% growth means steep deceleration is already the base case. Key debates: durability of $725B-to-$1T hyperscaler capex, revenue quality given 54% three-customer concentration, and whether China is a free option or permanently stranded.

scenarios.bear: 2027 hyperscaler capex flattens as AI ROI questions bite; custom ASICs take incremental inference share; China stays zero; growth decelerates to teens by FY2028, gross margin slips below 70%; multiple de-rates toward high-teens on cyclical reclassification.
scenarios.base: Rubin ramps on schedule H2 2026; hyperscaler capex grows into 2027 (~$1T); Data Center revenue +35-45% in FY2028 at ~75% gross margin; China negligible; stock compounds roughly with earnings at a low-20s forward multiple.
scenarios.bull: Rubin's ~5x uplift accelerates replacement cycles; agentic inference demand scales faster than training; China unlock adds a low-double-digit revenue layer; FY2028 estimates rise materially and the multiple re-rates toward high-20s/30s.

valPresets.note: Growth presets are year-1 rates that fade to terminal: base (30% fading) roughly matches the ~18% constant growth the reverse DCF says is priced in.
